method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)' (published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026)), 14 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC13268836). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9) 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance' (published 20 September 2021), 12 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC8563639). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, European expert practical guidance (consensus of 11 European authors reached at a virtual advisory-board meeting funded by EUSA Pharma, the maker of dinutuximab beta) on the SIOPEN dinutuximab beta regimen and its toxicities; S1 claims and anchors are unchanged. Searches (Europe PMC, 2026-09-24): neuroblastoma guideline/consensus/recommendation titles 2016-2026 and SIOPEN/COG treatment guidance. Found and not usable: NCCN Neuroblastoma 2.2024 (unusable terms), ICMR 2017 consensus and the French SFCE relapse guidelines (closed access), the 2025 Latin American anti-GD2 consensus (JCO Global Oncology, CC BY-NC-ND; ascopubs.org returned a Cloudflare 403, not bypassed), SIOPEN 2026 imaging recommendations (imaging only). No open SIOPEN or COG whole-pathway treatment guideline was found.

claims.claim: **Neuroblastoma is a cancer of the autonomic nervous system** that causes about 15% of childhood cancer deaths; it is rarer in adolescents and adults.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **'High-risk' is assigned from imaging stage, age, chromosomal changes and pathology.** Treatment combines intensive chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy, autologous stem-cell transplant and immunotherapy.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Relapse is common: more than 50% relapse** even after intensive multimodality treatment.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk group (S2):** set by age at diagnosis (cut-off 18 months), the tumour's histology and its molecular features: MYCN amplification, segmental chromosome changes and ploidy.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **About 50% of neuroblastomas are high-risk, with survival below 50%** despite multimodal treatment (induction chemotherapy and surgery, then high-dose chemotherapy and an autologous stem-cell transplant, radiotherapy and differentiation therapy). Adding an anti-GD2 antibody (dinutuximab, COG ANBL0032 trial) lifted survival above 60% (S2).
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **SIOPEN standard of care: dinutuximab beta by long-term continuous infusion (100 mg/m² over 10 days), without IL-2,** for patients who responded to induction and consolidation. The slower infusion caused less pain, allergy and hypotension than the 8-hour, 5-day schedule; adding IL-2 raised toxicity and did not improve survival.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Most dinutuximab beta adverse effects occur during the infusion and settle when it ends.** Pausing the infusion to give supportive care does not appear harmful; treat with supportive measures first, before reducing or interrupting doses, and prepare parents for what to expect.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No corticosteroids from 2 weeks before the first dose to 1 week after the last,** except in life-threatening situations (the experts also allow them for adrenal insufficiency and asthma). For anaphylaxis or transverse myelitis, stop the infusion at once and discontinue permanently.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pain: give triple therapy** (a non-opioid such as paracetamol or ibuprofen throughout, gabapentin, and morphine). Gabapentin is built up before the infusion: 10 mg/kg/day starting 3 days ahead; on the following day, 10 mg/kg twice (2 × 10); from the eve of the infusion, 10 mg/kg three times (3 × 10), kept until the cycle ends.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Morphine:** start a 0.02–0.05 mg/kg/h IV infusion before the antibody, or a 0.05–0.1 mg/kg bolus 2 h before it; then about 0.03 mg/kg/h during the infusion. Wean over no more than 5 days, finishing by the end of the first cycle's infusion and within 3–5 days of starting the second. Aim for the lowest dose for the shortest time; IV ketamine can be added for uncontrolled pain.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Fever is expected:** paracetamol can be given to prevent it. Take blood cultures when fever occurs, but empirical antibiotics are not advised for fever alone, even with a mildly raised CRP, unless the child is neutropenic or infection is clinically suspected.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allergy:** premedicate with an IV antihistamine about 20 min before each infusion, repeated every 4–6 h if needed (or regular oral antihistamine from the day before). Grade 1–2 reactions: pause, treat and restart. Grade 3–4 anaphylaxis: stop permanently and give IV antihistamine, adrenaline and steroids.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Capillary leak:** watch blood pressure and weight; mild leak may need no treatment, otherwise manage fluids by weight, blood pressure and local protocol. Use diuretics cautiously because of hypotension; furosemide suits marked weight gain with pulmonary oedema or ascites when blood pressure is normal.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transverse myelitis: stop the infusion immediately and never restart dinutuximab beta;** give IV immunoglobulin and high-dose steroids. Children with severe neuropathy should not be rechallenged even after full recovery.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Raised liver enzymes without symptoms need no action:** below 20 times the upper limit of normal, monitor closely and keep the dose; avoid hepatotoxic drugs.
claims.locator: Barone G, Barry A, Bautista F, et al., van Noesel MM (European experts in neuroblastoma immunotherapy), Paediatric Drugs 23(6):537-548 (doi 10.1007/s40272-021-00469-9), 'Managing Adverse Events Associated with Dinutuximab Beta Treatment in Patients with High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Practical Guidance', published 20 September 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8563639/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Eflornithine is an oral maintenance drug to lower relapse risk** for patients whose disease has at least partly responded to earlier multiagent, multimodality treatment.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It works by irreversibly blocking ornithine decarboxylase,** the key enzyme in polyamine synthesis.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Evidence: a matched comparison of 90 treated patients with 270 historical controls,** all under 21 with at least a partial response. Event-free survival HR 0.48 and overall survival HR 0.32 favoured eflornithine; four-year survival was 96% versus 84%.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The trial was externally controlled, not randomised,** so the result is uncertain; sensitivity analyses gave similar answers.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Place in therapy:** an added option that may improve survival after at least partial response to induction and consolidation (including immunotherapy), with toxicity that needs ongoing monitoring.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral, twice a day, dosed by body surface area:** from 192 mg (1 tablet) up to 768 mg (4 tablets) per dose. Continue for 2 years, or until recurrence or unacceptable toxicity. Lower doses can be used for adverse effects.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reduce the dose in severe renal impairment** (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²).
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tablets can be chewed, or crushed into a little liquid,** for children who cannot swallow them.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Main serious harms: liver toxicity, neutropenia, anaemia and hearing loss.** Ear, chest and skin infections, conjunctivitis, cough, diarrhoea and vomiting are also common.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check full blood count, liver function and hearing before starting and periodically during treatment.**
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pregnancy category B3.** Patients (or partners) who could conceive need effective contraception while on treatment and until 1 week after the final dose; there are no lactation data.
claims.locator: Australian Prescriber, Aust Prescr 2026;49(3):112, 'Eflornithine for neuroblastoma (new drug comment)', published 2 June 2026 (finalised 13 April 2026), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13268836/, retrieved 2026-09-23
